newsitem.title: USA: Tanzanian student accused of molesting girl scouts.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian student accused of molesting girl scouts.

text.p: Police were considering charges on Wednesday against a female exchange student from Tanzania who allegedly sexually molested campers at a Girl Scout camp where she was a counsellor.
"We haven't filed any charges against her because we're still trying to put the pieces together," Hamilton Township Police Chief Eugene Duvelius told reporters.

The 19-year-old suspect allegedly fondled the breasts and buttocks of more than a dozen 10- and 11-year-old girls at the Camp Butterworth Girl Scout camp in this historic village 20 miles (32 km) northeast of Cincinnati.
After the girls reported the incidents, camp supervisors ordered the counsellor to leave and she boarded a bus bound for New York on Monday, authorities said.

Warren County prosecutor Rachel Hutzell said authorities were only notified 12 hours after the alleged molestations were discovered and camp supervisors could be criminally liable for not turning the girl over to police.
Roni Luckenbill, assistant executive director of the Great Rivers Girl Scout Council that runs the camp, said the Tanzanian student was ordered to leave because "we had to take her out of that camp."
Luckenbill said camp supervisors first informed parents about the incidents before contacting police because they felt that was a priority.
"Our investigation was severely hampered by their failure to hold the counsellor for police," Hutzell told Reuters. "We understand she is not in custody but has retained legal counsel in New York."
